cases.statement: One person: Patient 5 of a nine-patient retrospective series; onset at 7 months with tremor, later steroid-responsive course.

people.label: Patient 5
people.key_phenotypes: intention tremor of hands and head tremor from 7 months; vomiting, failure to thrive, dysphagia, dysarthria; sleep apnoea and respiratory insufficiency needing resuscitation once; absence seizures; pyramidal signs and ataxic gait; typical MRI features

except for patient 5, for whom the disability grade, the mark “aG”, and the level of care might have not been adjusted after the patient was able to walk again without his wheelchair.
Patient 5 was initially classified as an atypical AxD case, presenting with an intention tremor of the hands and tremor of the head at the age of seven months as first symptoms.
Typical MRI features were found.

During the course of the disease the patient experienced episodes of vomiting and failure to thrive, as well as dysphagia and dysarthria, sleep apnoea, and respiratory insufficiency, leading to the necessity of resuscitation and ventilation on one occasion.
Epileptic seizures in form of absences were also treated with steroids and suspended under that therapy.
Pyramidal signs and an ataxic gait disorder were reported.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Typical MRI features reported, although the patient was first classified as atypical; the authors note MRI core features of only the bulbospinal type. No testing of other genes is described; the testing method is not stated.

quotes.quote: Typical MRI features were found.
Patient 5 was initially classified as an atypical AxD case, presenting with an intention tremor of the hands and tremor of the head at the age of seven months as first symptoms.
From the remaining two patients, one (patient 5) had clinical core features of both types but only MRI core features of the bulbospinal type.

de_novo.statement: Authors state that two of the three novel variants arose de novo; by exclusion of c.209G>C these are c.1118A>G and c.1013T>C, and the authors' criteria list for c.1013T>C includes the de novo criterion. Which parents were tested and whether parentage was confirmed are not reported.

quotes.quote: Two of these variants arose de novo, while for the third (c.209G>C, patient 7), no segregation data was available.

According to ACMG guidelines, the variants c.1118A>G (PM1, PP2, PM2, PM5, PP3, PS2) and c.1013T>C (PM1, PP2, PM2, PP3, PS2) were classified as pathogenic variants, while the variant c.209G>C was classified as likely pathogenic (PM1, PP2, PM2, PM5, PP3) [30].

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense, p.(Leu338Pro), exon 6 per the paper. Authors state it lies in a mutational hotspot region; general mechanism stated as gain of function.

quotes.quote: We identified three GFAP gene variants, which had not been published to date: c.1118A>G (p.Glu373Gly) and c.1013T>C (p.Leu338Pro), both in exon 6, (the latter is described by A. Messing as an unpublished variant, without neuropathological confirmation [27]), and c.209G>C (p.Arg70Pro) in exon 1.
They were predicted to be non-truncating on the protein level but leading to non-synonymous amino acids alteration located in mutational hotspot regions [30].
The pathogenic gene variants are in most cases de novo missense variants, leading to a gain of function.

authors_classification.statement: Authors' ACMG call, made with the Franklin (Qiagen/Genoox) tool, quoted below.

quotes.quote: According to ACMG guidelines, the variants c.1118A>G (PM1, PP2, PM2, PM5, PP3, PS2) and c.1013T>C (PM1, PP2, PM2, PP3, PS2) were classified as pathogenic variants, while the variant c.209G>C was classified as likely pathogenic (PM1, PP2, PM2, PM5, PP3) [30].
Novel GFAP variants were classified according to the recommendations of the ACMG by using Franklin by Qiagen/Genoox [29,30].

concerns: Authors say this variant is listed by A. Messing (Waisman Center/Zenodo variant list) as an unpublished variant without neuropathological confirmation; that listing may refer to this same patient, so it should not be counted as an independent observation.
The de novo statement does not name the variants explicitly (only by exclusion) and gives no details of parental testing or parentage confirmation.
Criteria assigned with an automated tool (Franklin).
Transcript not stated in the paper. Atypical, steroid-responsive course with marked improvement.
notes_for_panel: Single case; table footnote marks the variant as present in Messing's unpublished list (quote: Table 1 'unpublished' row 'X *' and footnote). Footnote text: see concerns.
